lede: Pittsburgh Steelers carries the stronger EdgeDesk offensive profile (#25 in EPA per play), while Cleveland Browns owns the more favourable defensive matchup (#7 in EPA allowed per play).
EdgeDesk’s independent projection makes it Cleveland Browns -0.5 with a fair total of 36.8 — approximately a one-score game, before any sportsbook number is consulted.

The widest measured matchup on the board is Pittsburgh Steelers pass offence vs Cleveland Browns pass defence, which sits −0.247 from the league mean once the two ratings are combined the way the model combines them.
The largest uncertainty is quarterback information: Pittsburgh Steelers and Cleveland Browns have no confirmed starter on file, which materially affects how much confidence the exact number deserves.
